newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds open weaker amid strong U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds open weaker amid strong U.S. data.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened weaker in moderate trade on Tuesday, falling in tandem with U.S. treasuries, amid stronger than expected U.S. manufacturing data for March, analysts said.

"The manufacturing report that was released this morning was a little bit stronger than what some had expected," said Garett Prins, a fixed-income analyst with J.P. Morgan Canada. "(Canadian bonds) are probably trading off of the treasuries, which are also off.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.55 to C$107.45 to yield 7.351 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 17/32 to yield 7.14 percent. The spread between the two bonds narrowed to 21 basis points to 22 basis points.

Both Canadian and U.S. debt markets weakened after the U.S. Federal Reserve reported industrial production rose 0.9 percent in March, compared with expectations of a 0.6 percent rise. The Fed also reported that capacity utilization rose to 84.1 percent, compared with an 83.6 percent forecast.
The data increased speculation that the U.S. Federal Reserve will hike interest rates as early as May, putting pressure on both Canadian bond markets and the currency.
In other prices, the Canadian 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.33 to C$101.17 to yield 6.831 percent. The U.S. bond fell 12/32 to yield 6.93 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds widened to 10 basis points from eight basis points on Tuesday.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.23 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.30 percent.
